主要内容: The State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) is a U.S. government program aimed at supporting small businesses through credit support and investment programs. The initiative was funded by the American Rescue Plan Act, signed into law on March 11, 2021, which allocated $10 billion to support state, territory, and Tribal government programs. The SSBCI program focuses on catalyzing investment in underserved entrepreneurs and venture capital fund managers. The Treasury Department has released various resources, including a guidebook on communications and media relations, and has launched an application portal for the Technical Assistance Grant Program. The program has also undergone several deadline extensions for tribal governments and states, with the latest updates as of 2022. The initiative is part of broader efforts to support small business growth and economic recovery. The U.S. Department of the Treasury has been actively involved in supporting small businesses through the State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI), which aims to provide financing and technical assistance to small businesses, particularly in underserved communities. The initiative has supported over $3.1 billion in new financing for small businesses, with additional funding allocated to tribal governments and states. The Treasury has also announced new funding for small businesses in various states and territories as part of the Biden-Harris Administration’s Investing in America Agenda. These efforts include technical assistance programs and funding for historically underserved entrepreneurs. The SSBCI has been a key part of the administration’s strategy to drive economic growth and support small business success across the United States. The U.S. Department of the Treasury has been actively supporting small business growth and entrepreneurship through the State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) as part of the Biden administration's Investing in America agenda. The initiative has allocated significant funds to various states, territories, and tribal governments to promote economic development and support underserved entrepreneurs. For instance, up to $353.4 million was approved for four states, and $339 million for three states and two U.S. territories. Additionally, Puerto Rico received up to $109 million to foster small business growth. The initiative also includes technical assistance programs, such as deploying $300 million in support for underserved entrepreneurs and very small businesses. The timeline includes key events like the release of the SSBCI Investing in America Small Business Opportunity Program (SBOP) NOFO and a pre-application webinar scheduled for November 6, 2023. The U.S. Department of the Treasury implemented the Social Security Benefits and Community Investment (SSBCI) program as part of the American Rescue Plan Act signed by President Biden on March 11, 2021. The program aimed to provide financial assistance to Tribal Governments, states, territories, and municipalities. Key dates included a Tribal Consultation on May 27, 2021, with responses due for the request for information on June 4, 2021. Preliminary allocation amounts were provided to Tribal governments by June 30, 2021. Applications for SSBCI capital programs from states, territories, and Washington, DC were initiated by December 11, 2021, and completed by February 11, 2022. Municipalities in states not applying for SSBCI had to submit applications by March 11, 2022. Technical assistance funding applications were due by October 14, 2022, and Tribal governments had to complete their applications by October 31, 2022. The comment deadline for the RFI was extended to November 3, 2022, allowing stakeholders to submit feedback on Regulations.gov.
